name: KeyboardSelect
summary: Each face of the polyhedron shows a number; turning the left palm towards oneself opens a number pad on which the right hand types the face's number.
howItWorks: Far-field aiming becomes a discrete key press, so hand jitter no longer matters. It was among the three best techniques, with low error rates, but finding numbers took time. Tested with 16 participants selecting single faces on regular polyhedra (4, 6 or 12 faces, two sizes) with tracked hands.
limitations: Slow to find numbers; less liked on complex models.

relationships.note: Introduced with seven other face-selection techniques in the same study.
The study's baseline (DragRotate) rotates the object with one hand and selects with a hand ray.
